Following last week’s release of Carbon and Hydrogen , Google today is rolling out Gemini 4 Neon. The model offers “frontier-level reasoning for complex, high-frequency workflows faster and more cost efficiently.” Before today, Google’s Gemini 4 family consisted of: Neon has performance comparable to, if not surpassing, Carbon across coding, reasoning, and agentic tasks, but at Flash speeds and a lower cost. As such, Neon is available in the Gemini app for AI Pro (and AI Ultra) subscribers, with 3.1 Pro finally going away. Neon also replaces Argon. Meanwhile, 3.5 Flash-Lite is now “Auto” in the model picker for paid users. Officially, the new model sits between Hydrogen and Carbon in the Gemini 4 family. Neon is built for complex coding, analytical reasoning, and production-grade enterprise workflows. While Carbon tackles your hardest, long-horizon projects and Hydrogen handles fast everyday execution, Neon balances depth and efficiency. In terms of benchmarks: Neon is priced at $3/1M input tokens and $15/1M output tokens, or twice as expensive as Hydrogen. Argon and Carbon cost $2/1M input and $10/1M output until November 30. After the promotional pricing, it will be $4/1M input and $20/1M output, with Neon 25% cheaper as a result. The model is also available in Google Antigravity for paid AI Pro or Ultra subscribers.
